issues.claim: Link titled "Объединение делегатов (многоадресные делегаты)" is cited for: an exception from one handler stops the invocation of the remaining handlers
issues.problem: The fetched excerpt says only that a multicast delegate "invokes the delegates in the list, in order" and shows the + and - operators. It says nothing about what happens when a handler throws. The answer hinge (the third subscriber is never called) therefore has no source in the excerpt. The generator notes say the same.
issues.suggestedFix: Add or swap in a source that states the behaviour. The best fit is the Delegate invocation section of the C# language specification (delegates chapter on Microsoft Learn, kind: spec). It says an uncaught exception in an invoked method propagates to the caller of the delegate. Keep the multicast page only for the 'in order' claim.

issues.claim: Link "Паттерн Декоратор (Refactoring.Guru)" is cited for: a decorator intercepts only calls that come through its own reference, and calls the inner object makes on itself bypass the wrapper
